_metadata.title: QIF non-adversarial hazards
_metadata.description: Non-adversarial hazards to people who use neural devices: conditions with no attacker, such as loss of support or gradual hardware change. They are kept apart from the attack techniques in qtara-registrar.json and are not counted as techniques. For threat modeling only. Proposed and unvalidated: not peer-reviewed as a set, not adopted by any standards body, and not a clinical or diagnostic instrument.

fields.bands: QIF hourglass band ids the hazard is tagged to
fields.related_techniques: QIF-T#### ids of registrar techniques that are adjacent to the hazard; a link is a pointer, not evidence
fields.sources: Citation strings for the hazard itself
fields.peer_review_status: peer_reviewed | preprint | none, derived from sources by the same rule as the registrar
fields.status: Registrar evidence vocabulary. An entry whose peer_review_status is preprint or none may not hold a status above THEORETICAL
fields.hazard_class: Optional grouping tag. 'environmental_operational' marks everyday, non-adversarial conditions (interference, moisture, heat, motion, power, contact, configuration) that can degrade a neural device or its signal without any attacker
fields.detection: Optional block for monitoring tools. 'signals' lists observable indicators; 'requires' lists the device capabilities needed to observe them; 'observability' states what a monitor may claim: observable (direct sensor exists), indirect (only correlated signal evidence; report as suspected, never confirmed), or user_report (not machine-observable). A monitor without the required capability must report the check as unavailable, never as normal or safe

hazards.name: Loss of manufacturer or sponsor support for an implanted neural device
hazards.description: A person keeps an implanted neural device after the party that maintains it withdraws. No one acts on the device and the neural signal is untouched; what changes is the support layer around it. Supported by the source: Higgins et al. 2026, a 24-expert modified Delphi study in an Australian context, reached consensus that post-trial responsibility for implantable neural devices needs explicit rules, motivated by the risk that access ends on trial failure, commercial non-viability or safety suspension. Zhao and Lin 2026 add a normative argument that long-term embodiment complicates consent to explantation. Not shown by either source: how often loss of support happens, or what harm follows. Projected, and not from the sources: that vulnerabilities on an unsupported device stay unpatched, or that a third party could exploit the gap. Paired control: a continuity plan agreed before implantation that names who maintains, funds, secures and, if needed, removes the device when the sponsor exits. The specific Delphi recommendations were not read; this entry rests on a summary of the papers, not their full text.
sources: Higgins et al. 2026 (BMC Med Ethics; 24-expert modified Delphi on post-trial responsibility for implantable neural devices) DOI:10.1186/s12910-026-01475-7
Zhao, Lin 2026 (BMC Med Ethics; normative analysis of consent to explantation) DOI:10.1186/s12910-026-01540-1

hazards.name: Chronic electrode micromotion (non-adversarial reading of QIF-T0120)
hazards.description: Pointer entry. The registrar holds QIF-T0120 as a technique, but the mechanism it records describes no adversary: movement of an implanted electrode over time, with change at the electrode-tissue interface and in recording or stimulation fidelity. That fits this file better than the technique list. QIF-T0120 has not been moved, because moving it would change the published technique count and existing references; the move is an open decision for the framework's author. No source is attached to QIF-T0120 and none was added here, so this entry asserts nothing about incidence, tissue response or any cognitive outcome, and the band tags are carried over from QIF-T0120 without review. Paired control, stated as a general practice and not drawn from a source: trend monitoring of electrode impedance and signal quality.

hazards.name: Moisture and liquid exposure (sweat, spills, humidity, condensation)
hazards.description: Everyday moisture around a worn or implanted-adjacent neural device: sweat accumulating under surface electrodes, rain or spills, high humidity, condensation after temperature change, or liquid entering a connector. Plausible effects, stated as general electronics and electrophysiology practice and not drawn from a verified source in this pass: changed electrode contact and impedance, corrosion or shorts in connectors, degraded or misleading recordings, and electrical risk where the hardware is not rated for the exposure. A signal change alone cannot confirm moisture; confirmation needs a moisture/humidity sensor, impedance telemetry, a device-reported fault, or a user report. Paired control: impedance and contact-quality trend monitoring where supported, manufacturer drying and inspection guidance, and pausing interpretation of affected channels. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

requires: impedance telemetry or contact-quality telemetry (for indirect evidence)

hazards.name: Static and low-frequency magnetic field exposure (magnets, motors, MRI environments)
hazards.description: Ambient magnetic fields from permanent magnets, magnetic clasps and mounts, motors, speakers, or high-field environments such as MRI suites. Effects are strongly device-dependent: magnetometers and magnetically sensitive components can be disturbed or saturated, while ordinary EEG electrodes are not a general-purpose magnetic field sensor, so a magnetic cause cannot be established from EEG channels alone. MRI is a special case: exposure of a device not cleared for that environment is a serious physical hazard governed by the manufacturer's MRI safety labeling; a software alert, or its absence, must never be treated as MRI clearance. Paired control: magnetometer or field-sensor thresholds where the hardware has one, device fault telemetry, and display of the manufacturer's documented MRI restrictions. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

signals: magnetometer or field-sensor reading beyond configured limit
correlated disturbance across magnetically sensitive channels
requires: magnetometer or dedicated field sensor (for observation); without one the hazard is at best suspected

hazards.name: Mains electrical interference and power-quality faults (50/60 Hz, ground loops, faulty chargers)
hazards.description: Everyday electrical interference coupling into acquisition: 50/60 Hz mains pickup and harmonics, broadband noise from nearby equipment, ground loops, poor shielding, damaged cables, static discharge, or a faulty charger. Mains contamination of biopotential recordings is standard measurement practice knowledge, though no source was verified in this pass. A spectral peak near the local mains frequency is consistent with mains interference but does not by itself establish the source; the observation and the attributed cause must stay separate. Paired control: notch/spectral monitoring of mains bands, clipping and common-mode indicators, device fault telemetry, and safe-configuration guidance. Controls must never advise defeating protective earth or opening powered equipment. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

signals: persistent spectral peak at local mains frequency and harmonics
requires: raw signal access with known sampling rate (spectral analysis)

hazards.name: Device overheating and battery thermal fault
hazards.description: Excessive device or battery temperature from charging while worn, blocked ventilation, hot environments, direct sunlight, or a degrading battery. Plausible effects, stated as general electronics practice: degraded electronics and measurements, skin discomfort or burn risk, and battery failure modes. Overheating cannot be confirmed from signal noise alone: confirmation needs temperature or battery telemetry or a device-reported fault, and a device without a temperature sensor must be reported as 'temperature monitoring unavailable', never as 'temperature normal'. Severe warning signs (swelling, smoke, burning smell) call for the manufacturer's stop-use and emergency guidance, not continued monitoring. Paired control: manufacturer thresholds with hysteresis on temperature and charge telemetry. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

requires: temperature or battery telemetry exposed by the device

hazards.name: Surface electrode contact degradation (dry gel, shift, hair, detachment)
hazards.description: Non-adversarial loss of recording contact on wearable or cap-based systems: dried conductive gel, dry electrodes losing pressure, hair obstructing contact, a shifted headband or cap, uneven pressure, or a detached electrode. Distinct from QIF-H0002, which records implanted electrode micromotion. Plausible effects: noisy, attenuated or misleading channels that can be mistaken for neural change. Paired control: per-channel impedance or contact-quality checks where the device supports them, flatline and dropout detection, cross-channel comparison, and user inspection prompts. A contact fault is a signal-integrity finding, not evidence of cognitive change or attack. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

signals: flatline or dropout on specific channels
requires: impedance/contact telemetry (direct) or raw per-channel signal (indirect)

hazards.name: Motion and vibration artifact (movement, cable tug, vehicle travel)
hazards.description: Movement-linked signal contamination: head and body movement, walking or running, cable tugging, mechanical vibration from vehicles or equipment. Motion artifact in biopotential recording is standard measurement practice knowledge, though no source was verified in this pass. Movement-related signal change must not be classified as neural abnormality; correlation with inertial measurements is the discriminator where an accelerometer exists. Paired control: accelerometer correlation, artifact-aware quality flags, and timing analysis between motion and signal events. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

signals: signal transients time-locked to accelerometer/IMU activity
channel dropout coinciding with cable strain
requires: accelerometer or IMU channel (for correlation); without one, motion is only suspected

hazards.name: Wireless link instability and RF congestion (Bluetooth/Wi-Fi packet loss)
hazards.description: Transport-layer degradation of a wireless neural device link: Bluetooth congestion, Wi-Fi interference, distance or body shadowing, reconnection loops, packet loss, latency and jitter. A transport fault and analog signal contamination are different failure modes and must not be conflated: lost packets make samples missing, they do not make the underlying neural signal wrong. Paired control: packet counters, sequence-gap detection, link-quality telemetry where exposed, and visible missing-sample accounting. Missing data must be marked missing, never silently interpolated. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

requires: transport telemetry or sequence-numbered sample stream

hazards.name: Power instability and battery depletion (brownouts, resets, unstable supply)
hazards.description: Non-adversarial power problems: low or degraded battery, unstable USB supply, charging faults, voltage excursions, and the resets or recording interruptions that follow. Distinct from QIF-H0027 (thermal) and from QIF-T0031, which records deliberate battery drain by an adversary. Paired control: battery and power telemetry where exposed, device error codes, and explicit incomplete-recording status after an interruption. Telemetry the device does not expose must be reported as unavailable, never invented. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

requires: battery/power telemetry or device status events

hazards.name: Environmental contamination and out-of-limit storage or use (dust, residues, temperature/humidity extremes)
hazards.description: Gradual environmental degradation: dust or debris in connectors, skin products or residues affecting electrode contact, condensation cycles, and storage or use outside the manufacturer's documented environmental limits. Most of these conditions are not directly machine-observable on common devices; where no sensor exists, the correct product behaviour is a transparent inspection checklist and a user-report pathway, not an unsupported detection claim. Paired control: manufacturer cleaning and storage guidance, periodic inspection prompts, and contact-quality trending as indirect evidence. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

signals: environmental sensor readings outside documented limits where fitted
requires: environmental sensors (rare) or longitudinal contact-quality records

hazards.name: Acquisition configuration and data-integrity faults (rate changes, dropped or duplicated samples, saturation)
hazards.description: Non-adversarial acquisition faults that corrupt the record without any attacker: sampling-rate or channel-map changes from reconfiguration or firmware updates, driver incompatibilities, buffer overflows, missing or duplicated samples, timestamp discontinuities, and amplifier saturation or clipping. These are deterministic, software-observable checks and belong in the first line of monitoring for any neural recording. An integrity fault makes downstream analysis unreliable and must gate interpretation: a record failing integrity checks may not be used as evidence of neural change or of an attack. Paired control: metadata validation, sequence and timestamp checks, sample-count reconciliation, configuration hashes, and clipping detection. No incidence or outcome claim is made.

signals: sampling-rate or channel-map mismatch against session metadata
requires: timestamped, sequence-numbered sample stream with declared configuration
